subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should `openclaw models status --probe` grow an opt-in all-configured-model live probe, or should configured-model/fallback validation be folded into another diagnostics workflow?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding this mode changes live provider-call behavior, output contracts, and operator expectations while overlapping related model/fallback diagnostics issues.

options.title: Define `--probe --all` contract
options.body: Approve a narrow status-probe flag that expands configured model candidates only when requested, with docs, JSON/status contract, and live proof before implementation lands.

options.title: Fold into broader model diagnostics
options.body: Keep this issue open as input to a fallback-chain or staged-migration diagnostics design instead of adding another status mode now.

options.title: Decline core live sweep
options.body: Leave per-model sweeping to external scripts or future plugin tooling, accepting that current status probes remain provider/auth focused.

recommendation.title: Define `--probe --all` contract
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow status-probe flag that expands configured model candidates only when requested, with docs, JSON/status contract, and live proof before implementation lands.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current auth probe surface and has the strongest recent history across provider identity and model status/probe behavior.
